title: Sequence length sweep - 96 frames
research_question: Does increasing sequence length from 64 to 96 frames improve WLASL30 recognition accuracy under the same GRU+Attention architecture?

hardware.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU

main_findings: Top-1 58.82% matches the notebook-11 reference number for the GRU+Attention WLASL30 run on the same split, and sits between the 32f (61.76%) and 64f (55.88%) seed=42 results.
Best epoch 29 (total 59) is the earliest of the three lengths, suggesting longer inputs either converge faster or overfit earlier with the current patience=30 setting.
Top-5 85.29% is close to the 32f run (88.24%) and well above the 64f baseline (73.53%), consistent with the Top-5 metric being less sensitive to individual test-sample swings.
limitations: Single seed; cannot tell whether 96f's earlier convergence is a repeatable effect or a one-off artefact of this seed.
Test set has only 34 samples, so per-metric deltas below ~3 pp are within single-sample noise.
96-frame inputs inflate per-batch memory and compute without an obvious Top-1 benefit in this run, but that conclusion cannot be generalised from a single seed.
next_actions: Re-run with seeds 123 and 2026 to confirm whether 96f consistently converges earlier and whether its Top-1 stays below 32f or crosses it.
If 96f stays on par with 64f after multi-seed aggregation, flag the extra frames as not justified by the memory and compute overhead for this dataset size.
